items.evidence: "Andrei presented the new UniMile rooms"; "The university allocated contiguous rooms on UniMile's sixth floor" with one-, two-, three-person rooms.
Notes cover furniture and the reading/lounge room's effect on positions, but not the question of whether per-room counts are strict, nor Susan's question of whether the lounge is needed at all.
Furniture and photocopier/fax/printer constraints are noted; the question of what happens if the group does not get the space (or more people are added) is not.
"Colleagues met to plan how to use newly allocated office space"; sections on arrangement options.

Notes cover professors sharing with students, project grouping, phone calls, splitting rooms for privacy, meeting rooms for projects, visitors, smoking, Gisela's placement and admin space. Smoking is covered only as no longer a constraint, not where to smoke.
No mention of the cafeteria or coffee machines.
Action item: "Find out whether the rooms can be separated, including the required authorization (owner: Andrei)".
No mention of asking about putting Gisella with the school's other admin.
"planned to bring individual preferences and a draft proposal to a follow-up"; "participants should give their own preferences".
"Andrei asked participants to gather preferences and bring a sketch or coherent proposal."
"bring a sketch or coherent proposal".
"Another group is developing a separate allocation proposal for later comparison"; merging the two proposals is not stated explicitly.
"Ask Maggie and Pierrette about their office preferences (owner: Susan)".
"The group discussed meeting the following Tuesday afternoon, around 2 p.m."
"The group leaned away from project-based seating"; "may not hold up as projects and assignments change".

The transcript shows no decision: Speaker D objected that putting a visitor in the admin office is unrealistic, and Andre said he would try to find out. The notes say Gisela's placement is "unresolved" and that a two-person room's "second position would need a purpose", which matches the transcript.
Nothing about there being no cafeteria.
Notes do not raise whether the number of people per room can be changed (for example, squeezing four into a three-person room).
"preferences and constraints still need to be gathered"; the preferences section.
Notes discuss professors sharing with students/assistants and project-based seating.
"Susan proposed asking whether a two-person room could be split for more privacy"; Andrei to check. Cubicles are not mentioned.
The lounge's purpose is discussed ("reading room, meeting space, or overflow"), but not the question of whether it is needed at all.
"Only one position may remain free for a visitor or intern"; the lounge as visitor overflow.
"Gisela's administrative phone work makes room placement a specific constraint."
"A single-person room could accommodate the administrative work. A two-person room was another option..."
No mention of a cafeteria.
No mention of coffee machines.
